key_insight: Backtesting LLM forecasters can be misleading because models may "cheat" by seeing post-event information through retrieval or by being trained on data that already includes the event. Hindcast proposes replaying prediction markets in a way that helps evaluate forecasts without leaking the answer.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the evaluation problem for LLM-based forecasting systems: standard backtests can overestimate performance when future information enters via web retrieval or training data contamination.
method: Replay resolved prediction-market questions to simulate the forecasting context before outcomes were known.
Account for two leakage channels: retrieval of post-event reports and training-data temporal leakage across model generations.
Use hindcasting as an evaluation framework to more faithfully measure whether an LLM could have made the forecast at the time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves trustworthiness of benchmark results for forecasting models and helps distinguish genuine predictive ability from information leakage. It also encourages fairer evaluation practices for time-sensitive tasks.

paper_title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
paper_authors: Xiao Ye, Jacob Dineen, Evan Zhu, Shijie Lu, Kevin Song
